source_text: Certe quam mihi laeta iila, quam exoptabilis dies est, cum misericordiae Domini fauore arcessitione dilata senectam istam meam proferre contigerit, ut et orationibus sanctorum impense et iugiter deprecantium Dominum Christi martyrem uideam, ut coronam iustitiae quae tibi penes Dominum deposita est portare conspiciam. nec putaueris autem martyrii tibi secundum praesens uotum desiderii nostri gloriam tribui. tunc inde felicitatis huius conlata dignatio est, tunc iudicio suo iusto Dominus elegit destinatum martyrem, cum te exemptum de iustorum grege atque adsumptum sibi de inopinato constituit altario sacerdotem. praeclara prorsus et gloriosa uocationis electio et de Domini dignatione noua atque inaudita et mini felicitas transmarinae peregrinationis necessitatibus occupatum ad destinatum tibi munus ignarum ac nescium repente uenisse atque ita regressus tui tempus ad hoc esse libratum, ut insperata celeritate ueniendi intellegeres atque dinosceres honorem sacerdotii caelestis inter ceteros tibi potissimum destinatum et quod iussione Domini exspectatus uenires atque occurreres reseruatum. ut ecclesiae suae Dominus tota miserationis pietate consuleret, dimicationis plebis mora quem potius eligeret episcopum te quaerenti populo suo Christus inopinatum repente obtulit . et complacitum sibi caelestis prouidentia manifeste aduentus tui improuisa occursione monstrauit: documentum repentini ac pernicis occursus procurationem Dei uoluntatis ostendit, ut quod difficili expeditione uix potuisset occurrere celeritate facili perfectum sit urguentis Domini iussione et ut prius te in ecclesia Dei episcopum stare conspiceres et stuperes quam uenisse dinosceres.
thought_title: The joy of Vigilius's sudden election
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius directly, rejoicing that he has lived to see Vigilius unexpectedly made bishop and destined for martyrdom.
pass_a_gloss: Certainly how joyful that day is for me, how desirable, when it has happened that I prolong this old age of mine by the favor of the mercy of the Lord, with the delay of the summons extended, so that I may see the martyr of Christ, with the prayers of the saints earnestly and continually beseeching the Lord, so that I may behold you carrying the crown of righteousness which has been laid up for you with the Lord. But do not think that the glory of martyrdom is granted to you according to the present wish of our desire. Then the granting of this happiness was conferred, then the Lord by his just judgment chose a destined martyr, when he took you out from the flock of the righteous and, taken up to himself, unexpectedly made you a priest at the altar. Truly the election of your calling is splendid and glorious, both new and unheard of from the Lord's condescension, and for me it is happiness that, occupied by the necessities of a journey overseas, you came suddenly to the office destined for you, ignorant and unaware, and thus the time of your return was so balanced that by the unhoped-for swiftness of your coming you understood and recognized that the honor of the heavenly priesthood was destined for you especially among others, and that, awaited by the Lord's command, you came and met what was reserved. So that the Lord might care for his church with all the piety of his compassion, Christ unexpectedly and suddenly offered you to his people who were seeking a bishop, while the delay of the people's struggle was deciding whom he should rather choose. And the heavenly providence clearly showed by the unforeseen arrival of your coming that you were pleasing to itself: the proof of your sudden and swift arrival showed the working of God's will, so that what could scarcely have happened by difficult expedition was accomplished with easy speed by the command of the urgent Lord, and so that you might see and be amazed that you stood as bishop in the church of God before you realized that you had come.

choices.english: with the delay of the summons extended
choices.why: Keeps the ablative absolute structure and the sense that the summons (death) has been postponed by God's mercy.
rejected: the summons having been put off

choices.why: Echoes the biblical phrase and the glossary's 'righteousness' for iustitia.
Captures the gracious lowering of the Lord toward the author and Vigilius; 'favor' alone loses the downward motion.
Renders the adverbial phrase naturally while keeping the surprise element central to the passage.
The glossary maps sacerdotium to 'priesthood'; sacerdotem here is the person holding that office, so 'priest' is consistent.
Preserves the paradox of speed that was not even hoped for, matching the author's emphasis on the suddenness.

pass_b_english: How glad, how longed-for that day will be for me when, by the mercy of the Lord's favor, if by the delay of my summons it should be granted me to prolong this old age of mine, so that through the prayers of the saints who earnestly and constantly entreat the Lord I may see a martyr of Christ, and behold you bearing the crown of righteousness that has been laid up for you with the Lord. Do not think, however, that the glory of martyrdom is being granted to you merely according to the present wish of our desire. The gracious favor of this happiness was conferred then, and the Lord in his just judgment chose you as a destined martyr then, when he took you out from the flock of the righteous and, taking you up for himself, unexpectedly made you a priest at his altar. Splendid indeed and glorious is this election of your calling, and new and unheard-of in the Lord's condescension. And for me it is a happiness that you, occupied with the necessities of an overseas journey, came suddenly to the office destined for you, ignorant and unaware, and that the time of your return was so balanced that by the unhoped-for swiftness of your coming you understood and recognized that the honor of the heavenly priesthood was destined for you above all others, and that you came because you were awaited by the Lord's command, and arrived to meet what had been reserved for you. So that the Lord might provide for his church with all the loving-kindness of his mercy, Christ, while the people were delayed in the struggle of choosing whom they should elect as bishop, suddenly and unexpectedly offered you to his people as they sought. And the heavenly providence showed plainly that you were pleasing to him by the unforeseen arrival of your coming: the proof of your sudden and swift arrival showed the working of God's will, so that what could scarcely have happened through difficult effort was accomplished with easy speed by the urging command of the Lord, and so that you saw yourself standing as bishop in the church of God and were astonished before you knew that you had arrived.

problems.quote: the delay of my summons is extended
problems.source_quote: arcessitione dilata senectam istam meam proferre contigerit
problems.why: It is the delay of the summons that lets him prolong his old age, not the delay itself being extended.
problems.fix: the delay of my summons allows me to prolong this old age of mine
problems.ruling: Latin 'arcessitione dilata' = 'by the delayed summons', not 'the delay of my summons is extended'

edits.old: the delay of my summons is extended and I am allowed to prolong this old age of mine
edits.new: the delay of my summons allows me to prolong this old age of mine

fixed: Corrected: the source says 'arcessitione dilata senectam istam meam proferre contigerit' — the delay of the summons is the means by which he prolongs his old age, not something itself being extended. The English now reads 'the delay of my summons allows me to prolong this old age of mine.'

problems.quote: the delay of my summons allows me to prolong this old age of mine
problems.source_quote: arcessitione dilata senectam istam meam proferre contigerit
problems.why: Source says 'if it should happen' (contigerit) — a conditional/wish, not a flat statement.
problems.fix: if by the delay of my summons it should be granted me to prolong this old age of mine
problems.ruling: Latin contigerit (subjunctive) shows conditional, English renders as certain 'allows'.

edits.old: the delay of my summons allows me to prolong this old age of mine
edits.new: if by the delay of my summons it should be granted me to prolong this old age of mine

fixed: Source 'contigerit' is a perfect subjunctive expressing a wish or possibility ('if it should happen'), not a flat statement; the English 'allows me' loses this conditional force, so I restored it with 'if ... it should be granted me'.

last_rejected.why: 'Dominum Christi martyrem' = 'the Lord Christ as a martyr-witness'; 'Dominum' is accusative of 'Lord', not 'Lord's'.
last_rejected.fix: the Lord Christ as a witness
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'Dominum Christi martyrem' = 'a martyr of Christ'; translation matches meaning.
